- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward by ≤ 5% to prevent premature bottoming.  
- After a recent spike (last 3–5 prices > mean), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast slope for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.2–0.5) and forecast deviates > 5% from recent 7-day average, revert toward mean reversion.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast for last 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +0.8 → -0.5 → +0.6), model should adjust forecast mid-horizon to align with sentiment momentum.
